frequency_question: How often do executive agencies successfully finalize major announced fee or cost regulatory actions within a 12-month evaluation window when prioritized by leadership?
membership_rule: Includes major proposed rules by executive departments targeting fee increases or cost burdens published in the Unified Agenda where agency leadership signals high priority; excludes purely congressional statutes and rules dropped due to leadership changes.

cases.name: DHS Public Charge Rule Fee and Threshold Adjustments (2019)
USCIS Premium Processing Fee Schedule Final Rule (2020)
DOS/DHS Fee Schedule for Consular and Visa Services (2023)
USCIS Immigration Fee Schedule Major Revision (2024)
EPA Clean Power Plan Repeal and Replacement Rulemaking (2019)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 named cases representing major high-priority fee and regulatory actions by executive agencies; all reached final rule publication within their target windows.
known_gaps: Does not account for judicial injunctions or subsequent vacatur post-publication, only the official finalization event by the agency.
skeleton: Executive priority regulatory finalizations tracked across recent administrative cycles divided by total high-priority published financial rules.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 5 named major analogous priority rules where executive intent and capacity were aligned to drive completion.
validity_reason: Valid for the duration of the current presidential term as agency procedural capacity and leadership prioritization dynamics remain constant.
